_about: StickyMilk recipe photo style: 'home kitchen plus'. Every generated photo = house_style + one vessel + one money-shot moment + a fresh mix of background staging. Tune the words here; no code changes needed. Anchor photos in content/brand/anchors/ are sent with every request as the style reference.
house_style: A real but tidy home kitchen photographed on a bright morning, as if by the same food photographer in the same kitchen for a whole series.
The drink sits on a light oak butcher-block counter; behind it, softly out of focus, a warm off-white wall (#FEF8F4 cream) and a hint of white tile backsplash.
Soft natural window light from the left, gentle shadows falling to the right. Warm, bright and airy. No flash, no spotlighting, no dramatic contrast.
Camera slightly above the drink (about 15-25 degrees), 50mm lens look, shallow depth of field: the drink is tack sharp, the background soft.
Warm natural colors: cream, oak, espresso brown, milk white, with at most one small cobalt-blue (#001EC0) accent.
Real texture (condensation on cold glass, microfoam bubbles, clear ice) but never messy.
never: text, labels, logos or brand packaging
coffee machines, espresso machines, portafilters, grinders or coffee beans
cafe counters, chalkboards or menu boards
dark or moody backgrounds, heavy vignettes, oversaturated colors
art_director_rules: Describe the classic, expected presentation of this drink: the version people picture when they hear its name, styled beautifully. Don't reinvent it.
The tell must be obvious even at thumbnail size.
Be precise about liquid colors (a stirred latte is light tan, not espresso brown).
Choose the vessel only from the allowed list.

The story prop must be an ingredient of the recipe or simple tableware. Never brewing equipment (phin filters, moka pots, pour-overs, espresso or coffee machines, grinders, coffee beans), never text or packaging with visible labels, never cultural clichés (flags, hats, costumes).
Only use stages (before/after) when the drink is genuinely served or shown in two looks, e.g. layered then stirred.

vessels.hot_milk: a matte white ceramic cup (about 8 oz) on a matching saucer
vessels.iced: a tall clear faceted glass (about 14 oz) with clear ice cubes
vessels.short_faceted: a short, chunky clear faceted tumbler (about 8 oz)
vessels.double_wall: a clear double-wall glass, the drink seeming to float inside

moments.pour_swirl: The money shot: the coffee has just been poured over the cold milk and is cascading down through it, dark ribbons of espresso swirling into the white milk around the ice, caught mid-swirl.
moments.cold_foam: A thick, glossy cold foam cap sits on top, just starting to cascade at the edges into the coffee below.
moments.latte_art: Glossy microfoam with a simple latte art heart or rosetta on top.
moments.cappuccino: A tall, thick cap of foam on top.
moments.layered_tonic: Distinct layers: clear sparkling tonic with visible bubbles over ice below, dark espresso floating on top.
moments.affogato: Hot espresso just poured over a scoop of ice cream, melting into it at the edges.
moments.condensed_milk: A thick, creamy band of sweetened condensed milk visible at the bottom of the glass beneath the coffee.
moments.black_coffee: Rich dark coffee with a faint light-brown crema at the edge.
moments.iced_layers: Coffee and cold milk over ice in soft marbled layers, the coffee darker toward the top.

compositions: Medium shot. Drink slightly left of center on the counter; staging to the right and behind it.
Medium shot. Drink slightly right of center; staging to the left and behind it.
Close-up: the drink fills most of the frame, cropped just above the rim and below the base; only a hint of one prop at the edge.
Wider shot showing more of the kitchen: the drink in the front-left third, staging spread across the back of the counter.
Drink placed a little further back on the counter, with one prop in the soft-focus foreground at the frame's edge.
Straight-on at counter height, the drink centered, props low on either side, the backsplash visible behind.
